references.text: The Lord was angry with Israel and gave them into the hand of Cushan-Rishathaim, demonstrating God's wrath against disobedience, as seen in Deuteronomy.
Israel was taken from their land to Assyria because of their sins, a direct fulfillment of the warning that they would be cast out to another land.
The Lord rejected the entire house of Israel and gave them into the hand of plunderers, paralleling the wrath and anger described in Deuteronomy.
The Lord's anger led to Jerusalem and Judah being cast away from his presence, fulfilling the prophecy that they would be driven out to another land.
Moses had previously warned that the people would be scattered among the nations if they were disobedient, the same theme found in chapter 29.
The Lord warned that he would uproot them from their land and scatter them among all peoples, a direct parallel to being cast out to another land.
Stephen quotes the prophecy that Israel would be taken into exile in Babylon because of their idolatry, fulfilling the warning in Deuteronomy.
